newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Late S.African bonds cheery, rand retraces.
newsitem.headline: Late S.African bonds cheery, rand retraces.

text.p: South African bonds pierced the key 14 percent level in upbeat Thursday dealings, with demand driven mainly by continued interest rate cut hopes, option-related trade and strong U.S. Treasury bonds.
"The market was in buying mode and what we saw was a mini bull run," said a debt trader at a local brokerage.
"There was also quite a bit of option trading which pushed the market lower (ahead of the August 7 close-out)," he added.

At 1423 GMT the yield on the benchmark R150 bond had come off its intraday strongest levels of 13.935 percent -- its lowest since February 16 last year -- to trade at 13.96 percent from 14.03 percent at 1400 GMT on Wednesday.
Debt traders said the market consolidated around overnight levels during the morning despite the rand's woes.
It then broke below the 14 percent figure at midday, overcoming a major technical level at 14.01 percent, but bouncing off 13.935 percent on profit-taking.
Traders said there was more downside potential on Friday with 14.01 percent important to watch on the upside for any change in trend.
On Friday, players would also be watching out for the release of July gold and foreign exchange figures, due out at 1600 GMT.
June reserves came in at 22.13 billion rand.
The July numbers are seen benefiting from the proceeds of the Yankee bond issue in June and foreign bond purchases, but offset by Reserve Bank intervention in the forex market during the month.
Foreigners sold a net 69.05 million rands worth of South African bonds on Wednesday after buying 380.89 million rands on Tuesday, the Bond Exchange said.
Bond Exchange turnover rose to 11.98 billion rand on Wednesday from 11.62 billion rand on Tuesday.
The rand broke through 4.61 in hectic early trade to a fresh six month low, reaching a weakest intraday bid of 4.6140, on local imorter and speculative offshore dollar demand.
Major banks and smaller institutions said the Reserve Bank was not seen in the market smooting the unit's fall despite price action at one stage which suggested central bank activity.
The bank has been noticeable by its absence from the market during the week.
"It retraced some of the day's losses in the afternoon on exporter interest and some profit-taking," said a trader at a leading institution.
"Morning moves were fairly orderly," he added.
On Friday, the forex market was seen settling between 4.6050 to 4.6150. Technically, 4.6157 was seen a major level to break on the topside.
In cross rate action, the rand was last at 7.5449/5522 versus sterling from 7.4753/4848 on Wednesday, while against the mark it was last changing hands at 0.3989/3993 from 0.3987/3992 previously.
It was fetching 25.6830/7214 against the yen from a previous level of 25.6533/6810.
The South African Reserve Bank said the money market shortage fell to 5.912 billion rand on Wednesday from 6.587 billion rand on Tuesday.

Offered rates for three-month NCDs were fell further to between 15.40 to 15.50 percent from 15.45 to 15.55 percent, while the 90-day BA rate was also lower at 14.90 percent from between 14.90 to 15.00 percent previously.
-- Vera von Lieres, Johannesburg newsroom 27 11 482 1003
